review.evidence: R3 ProductCardReader.cs:26 and 36–56 uses null to encode unavailability and duplicates key canonicalization. CatalogCache.cs:32–44 leaves the retention and failure-time checks implicit. Public policy overloads have no XML contracts.

R3 CatalogCache.cs:28–32 and 61–85 names time thresholds and timestamps. R2 CatalogCache.cs:66–82 explains failure-time age and retention. Read XML leaves ineligible transient failure propagation implicit.

R3 ProductCardReader.cs:32–60 distinguishes original spelling, lookup key, and named outcomes. CatalogCache.cs:31–44 leaves fallback timing and timestamp preservation implicit. Batch XML summaries omit per-key error and exception details.

R2 CatalogCache.cs:49–67 explains failure-time age, why an entry must remain cached, and why fallback keeps the timestamp. R1 ProductCardReader.cs:24–38 covers order, spelling, error results, and exception propagation. R3 contracts track canonical identity and distinct null and blank errors.
Canonical JSON shape and reservedNames are readable. R3 ProfileCodec.cs:29–57 leaves URI delimiter checks and retry budget arithmetic in a long Parse method. Public XML contracts are absent.

R3 ProfileCodec.cs:54–56 names retryBudgetMs. R2 ProfileMigrator.cs:38–68 calls the success-only reservation set names. Public XML contracts and useful explanations of the URI delimiter checks are absent.

R3 ProfileCodec.cs:61–65 and 93–105 explain budget arithmetic, Int32 safety, and empty delimiters. R2 batch XML covers enumeration and error precedence. R1 DeploymentAdapter.cs:7 lacks a Create contract. The R3 adapter contract tracks the revised URL behavior.

R2 StockImporter.cs:121–146 explains zero keys and safe quantity differences. R3 StockImporter.cs:38–52, 65–78, and 115–147 explains EOF cancellation, issue precedence, tentative reservation, and publication. R3 StockStore.cs:67–74 uses committedOperationIds for tentative IDs too.

R2 StockImporter.cs:91–94 explains the safe Int32 difference. The R3 summary at lines 13–19 covers staging and rollback, with reader ownership and cancellation checkpoints left implicit. R3 ImportMode.cs:5 updates the mode documentation for the new timing.

ApplyRow separates validation from stream orchestration. R2 StockImporter.cs:82–104 explains EOF publication and explicit zero keys. R3 StockImporter.cs:40–56, 70–72, 109–119, and 153–170 documents cancellation and reserve-after-adjust, and updates partial-commit timing.

R1 DockDispatcher.cs:32 explains half-open boundaries. R2 DockDispatcher.cs:75–95 separates validation from mutation and rollback. R3 DockCalendar.cs:93 explains clipping, while the accumulator invariants at lines 105–138 are implicit. Public method XML is absent.

R1 DockDispatcher.cs:51–88 explains clipped endpoints, global IDs, earliest consecutive fit, and commit. R2 lines 98–139 explains why rollback preserves existing bookings. R3 DockCalendar.cs:135–196 explains shared occupancy and overlapping blackouts.

R2 DockDispatcher.cs:80–101 validates before mutation and rolls back only successful batch bookings. R3 DockCalendar.cs:89–152 leaves endpoint sweep, shared limits, and overlapping blackout handling unexplained. R3 has two accurate constructor summaries, with core method contracts absent.

R1 DockDispatcher.cs:49–113 distinguishes oversized valid requests from malformed input. R3 DockDispatcher.cs:80–125 explains prevalidation and rollback, with the repeat-ID case implicit in XML. R3 DockCalendar.cs:145–188 explains occupancy totals, blackout counts, and half-open endpoints.
